# [Test fixture] Alcohol intake and breast cancer incidence: a prospective cohort study

## Abstract

In this prospective cohort study of women followed for more than ten years, alcohol consumption was associated with a higher risk of breast cancer. The risk of breast cancer increased with the amount of alcohol consumed. Even light drinking was associated with a small increase in breast cancer risk compared with not drinking.

## Discussion

Alcohol is metabolised to acetaldehyde, which can damage DNA, and alcohol can raise oestrogen levels. These mechanisms may explain the association between drinking alcohol and breast cancer risk. Reducing alcohol consumption may lower the risk of breast cancer.
